name: Private credit stress
value: Nontraded BDC net outflows $4.1bn in Q3
summary: Nontraded BDCs saw $4.1bn net outflows in Q3 and a listed BDC sells at 90% of NAV; no wave of gates or bank losses
state: Preliminary Stanger data show redemptions from nontraded BDCs exceeded new capital by $4.1bn in the third quarter, while funds keep 5% quarterly redemption caps (Fixed Income News, 16 Nov). BC Partners agreed on 11 Nov to acquire Investcorp's listed BDC at 90% of adjusted NAV amid a sector shakeout (Bloomberg), and non-accruals are rising at some lenders. Searches on 16 Nov found no simultaneous wave of gates, forced asset sales or losses spreading to banks or insurers, so Watch holds.
for_you: Investors in semi-liquid private credit funds and BDCs are exposed to redemption limits and markdowns. Employees of mid-sized firms that borrow from these lenders are exposed if refinancing tightens.
rubric_hit: Watch: funds holding redemptions at 5% caps and listed BDCs at NAV discounts; no multi-fund gating or bank losses (Alert)

sources.title: Fixed Income News Australia — BC Partners deal signals consolidation as US private credit lenders feel the squeeze
Bloomberg — BC Partners to buy Investcorp BDC amid private credit shakeout

why: Private credit has grown fast outside bank regulation; its losses surface late and can spill into banks, insurers and pension funds.
drivers: Defaults among leveraged mid-sized borrowers, payment-in-kind interest, fund redemption requests, bank lending to funds.

rubric.alert: Several large funds gate at once, forced asset sales, or losses spreading to banks or insurers.
rubric.watch: A large fund limits redemptions, listed BDCs trade at wide discounts to NAV, or a cluster of borrower defaults with heavy losses.
rubric.normal: No notable fund gates, defaults or markdowns beyond the routine.
